correctness.rationale: Uniformly choosing one of the \(n+1\) suffix vertices gives the exact entrywise covariance and, by the Dirichlet Green identity, its tridiagonal inverse. The zero-extended compact Jacobi compressions converge in norm for each \(p\ge1\), hence the lower edge. The rescaled covariance step kernels converge uniformly to a weighted Brownian-bridge kernel; the Dirichlet Sturm-Liouville equation yields the Bessel upper edge. The claimed condition exponent follows from strictly positive limits at both edges, and the trace follows from an exact diagonal sum. Small-size exact fraction inversion and larger spectral computations have passed; infinite claims do not depend on computation.

value.rationale: For a canonical complete family of integer-weight lecture-hall simplices, the uniform-vertex Euclidean covariance has a distinct continuum upper edge and compact Jacobi hard edge. Their combination determines an arbitrary even polynomial anisotropy exponent \(2p+2\), even though all members are combinatorial simplices. The result is a motivated structural asymptotic classification with exact operator constants and a trace consistency law, rather than a finite table or a recomputation of the known Bessel process spectrum alone.
